clues: This town is the chief and most big town of its land. It holds more than a third of all the folk of the land.
In winter, bursts of ice-cold dry wind sweep in from the far south. They make the days feel raw and chill.
A fort post was set down here in 1723 by foes from the east. A chief of Spain threw them out, and the town dates its birth to 1726.
The head homes of two great trade blocs of its continent sit in this town. Folk liken its role to that of Brussels in Europe.
A world rank list has named this town the best place to live on its continent. It has held that rank each year since 2005.
